title: 'We gather here today with a lot of angst': Funeral for Niagara man shot by police
article: Fred Penner's death was described as a "horrific tragedy" during a funeral for the 56-year-old, Friday.
"We gather here today with a lot of angst," Rev. Valerie Kerr told dozens of friends and family at Hulse and English Funeral Home.
"We have questions. We're angry. We're afraid. We're in disbelief."
Penner died in hospital on Jan. 1, a day after being shot by Niagara Regional Police officers on Rykert Street following reports he was armed with a knife.
The shooting is now under investigation by the province's Special Investigations Unit.

"I would imagine that there's a lot of anger. I know I would be angry. So how do we deal with this anger?" added Kerr, archdeacon of the truth, reconciliation and Indigenous ministry for the Anglican Diocese of Niagara.
The family, she added, is not alone.
"My sense is that there's a whole community feeling those same feelings. They're angry. They have questions. They want to know why," she said.
Kerr told the family she prays they will find the answers they seek.

"The hard thing about that is, even when you get answers it's not going to bring Fred back," she said. "So, we have to figure out where we go from here. What would Fred want you to do with the rest of your life? How would Fred want you to deal with his untimely death?"
She urged Penner's friends and family not to allow the anger they feel to "eat you up."

"Don't let it make you bitter. Because I don't feel that that's what Fred would want," she said. "In the end, I'm sure what he would want is for you all to be happy. I know that's hard right now. I know it's hard to even think about being happy."
Penner's brother Marty recalled happy days they shared together.
He described Penner as "easy going," and "easy to talk to," and generous.
"That's why he's so well loved by the people who know him best," Marty said.
"The thing I will miss about Fred is the two of us playing guitar together, listening to the latest song or the lyrics he might be working on. ... Fred was very creative when it came to music."
Marty described the loss of his brother as "surreal" and "a bad nightmare."
"It feels like a part of me died along with Fred. ... Things will never be the same again."
Kerr referred to mental health struggles that plagued Penner in recent years.
Friends and family reported that Penner had been brought to the hospital for mental health issues at least twice in the week before his death.

"Even though he struggled in his own life, he still tried to care for other people. One of the things we don't talk about enough is our mental health. We don't talk about it. It's like we're ashamed if we have mental health issues. There's nothing to be ashamed of. It's when we talk about mental health that we can get help," Kerr said.
"This is a tragedy. A horrific tragedy. But together, we can do it by taking one step at a time."
